## Description {#details}

C++ header file with declarations for the µTest++ test reporter.

This header defines the <code>test&#95;reporter</code> class and related types, which are responsible for formatting and presenting test results within the µTest++ framework.

The <code>test&#95;reporter</code> class offers a comprehensive suite of output operators for various data types, containers, and comparator expressions, enabling detailed and informative reporting of test outcomes. It supports multiple verbosity levels and colour-coded output to distinguish between successful and failed tests.

The file also defines supporting types such as <code>colors</code> and <code>verbosity</code>, and provides methods for reporting the commencement and completion of test cases and suites, as well as for handling pass and fail conditions.

All definitions reside within the <code><Link to="/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus">micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus</Link></code> namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.

This file is intended solely for internal use within the framework and should not be included directly by user code.

The <code>verbosity</code> enumeration defines the available levels of detail for test output produced by the reporting system. These levels control the amount and type of information displayed during test execution, allowing users to tailor the output to their specific requirements.

Selecting an appropriate verbosity level enhances the usability of test reports, whether for concise summaries or comprehensive diagnostics.

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="stream">Reference to the <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/test-reporter">test&#95;reporter</Link></code> instance.</ParametersListItem>

The <code>endl</code> function inserts a newline character into the specified <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/test-reporter">test&#95;reporter</Link></code> stream and flushes its output buffer. This operation ensures that each test output line is clearly separated and immediately visible, facilitating the readability and clarity of test results across all test cases and folders within the µTest++ framework.
